The time it takes for a solar panel to become **carbon neutral**—meaning it has generated enough clean electricity to offset the greenhouse gases emitted during its manufacturing, transport, and installation—is typically referred to as its **energy payback time (EPBT)**.

### **Typical Energy Payback Time (EPBT)**
- **Modern solar panels:** **1 to 3 years**  
  - **Polycrystalline silicon:** ~1.5 to 2.5 years
  - **Monocrystalline silicon:** ~1.5 to 2 years (more efficient, but energy-intensive to make)
  - **Thin-film panels:** ~1 year (less energy used in manufacture, but often lower efficiency)

### **Factors Affecting the Carbon Payback**
- **Location & Sunlight:** Areas with more sunlight reduce payback time (more electricity generated).
- **Production methods:** Panels manufactured using dirtier grids (coal-heavy) take longer to offset their carbon footprint.
- **Panel efficiency:** Higher efficiency means faster payback.

### **Over Lifetime**
- Typical solar panels last **25–30 years** and generate **10-30 times** the energy used to make them.

---

**In summary:**  
**A solar panel generally becomes carbon neutral in 1 to 3 years**, after which all electricity it generates contributes to a net reduction of CO₂ emissions.

**References:**
- [National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL)](https://www.nrel.gov/docs/fy04osti/35489.pdf)
- [Fraunhofer Institute PV Report 2023](https://www.ise.fraunhofer.de/content/dam/ise/de/documents/publications/studies/Photovoltaics-Report.pdf)
- [IEA-PVPS Task 12](https://iea-pvps.org/key-topics/lca-of-pv/)
